_schema_comment: Idealized 1-D moisture-diffusion drying benchmark reconstructed from Xi, Bazant & Jennings (1994), Adv. Cem. Bas. Mat. 1:248-266 (Part 2, Figs. 15-16, Parrott 1988 drying test). Per CREATE.md: NOT a drop-in paper benchmark; model form is re-fit and several HIGH-impact values are assumed. RISKY - not validated until flagged items are confirmed.

metadata.title: Concrete drying - relative humidity history at several depths (Parrott 15 cm slab, w/c=0.58, Type I)
metadata.validation_method: reproduce Parrott (1988) drying: computed RH(t) at depths vs measured curves (paper Fig. 16, Part 2)
metadata.validation_target: RH(t) at 1.56 cm and 3.36 cm depths over 200 days
metadata.notes: RISKY: model-form caveats remain - (1) the S-curve is a fit to the paper's exponential D_h (max rel residual ~12%), (2) the surface film coefficient and initial RH are assumed, and (3) the paper's nonlinear moisture capacity is replaced by a constant (does NOT affect the RH solution, only water-content loss). D0=1.4e-11 m2/s is CALIBRATED against the digitized Parrott data (RMSE 0.026 RH). Reference curves are digitized from Fig. 16 (see reference/*.csv).
metadata.assumptions_report: See CREATE.md-required Assumptions Report in notes and _comment tags. HIGH-impact assumed/unknown: surface film coefficient (ASSUMED), initial RH (ASSUMED), D_h magnitude (CALIBRATED/MISSING), S-curve fit (CALIBRATED).

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE: Parrott drying specimen is a 15 cm (0.15 m) slab (Part 2, Fig. 16). In-plane height 0.10 m arbitrary; lateral faces x=0 and x=0.15 are the drying surfaces, top/bottom insulated so the field is effectively 1-D.

points._comment: PAPER_VALUE: Parrott sensor depth 3.36 cm (Fig. 16) - primary validation target

mesh._comment: recombine=false: recombine+refinement is a KNOWN ISSUE (dropped triangles -> singular matrix, 'N zero pivots', solution ~1e17). Coarse surface element 1 mm (was 0.5 mm) to cut node count. Field is quasi-1D so a modest mesh suffices.

humidity._comment: OOFEM BazantNajjarMoisture: C(h)=C1*[alpha+(1-alpha)/(1+((1-h)/(1-hc))^n)], governing eq dh/dt=div(C grad h). So D0 (c1) IS the effective diffusivity at saturation in m2/s. capacity does NOT divide C and does not affect the humidity solution - it is only used to convert RH change into water-content loss.
humidity._comment_fit: CALIBRATED: least-squares fit of the paper's D_h(H)=alpha_h+beta_h[1-exp(-gamma_h*10^(H-1))] at w/c=0.58 (Part 2 Eq. 4,7-9) to the S-curve shape. alpha_h=0.0436, beta_h=0.7705, gamma_h=6.9168. Fit: alpha=0.5266 (=D(0)/D(1)), hc=0.328, n=4.71. Max absolute residual 0.063, max relative residual ~12% over H in [0,1]. Shape ratios are unit-independent.
humidity._comment_D0: CALIBRATED: D0 (c1) = 1.4e-11 m2/s = 1.21 mm2/day, tuned to reproduce the digitized Parrott drying data (RMSE 0.026 RH over all depths/times). This is consistent with the paper's own D_h magnitude: at w/c=0.58, D_h(1)=alpha_h+beta_h ~ 0.81 (Fig. 8 axis in mm2/day), and the best fit lands slightly higher at ~1.2 mm2/day because of the assumed film coefficient / initial RH / S-curve shape. PREVIOUS value 30 mm2/day was ~25x too fast and gave no drying - replaced.
humidity._comment_capacity: INFERRED: paper moisture capacity dW/dH is nonlinear and not representable in bazant_najjar. Representative value ~0.14 g/g cement paste (mid-drying-range) x paste mass ~570 kg/m3 = ~80 kg/m3. Does NOT affect the RH solution (only water-content loss); RH validation is unaffected by this value.

initial_conditions._comment: ASSUMED: initial pore RH. Paper states hydration ceases near H~0.8 and inner pores stay near curing-room RH; a fresh saturated specimen is taken as 0.98. HIGH impact on early-time curves.

boundary_conditions._comment: ASSUMED: finite surface moisture transfer (Robin, not a Dirichlet shock). u_ref=0.50 from paper (Parrott drying at RH~50%). alpha=5e-8 m/s is a literature concrete surface moisture-transfer coefficient - HIGH impact, review.
ASSUMED: symmetric drying on the opposite face, same film coefficient.

dt_strategy._comment: t_end = 200 days x 86400 s/day. Log-spaced dt: fine near t=0 where drying starts fastest, coarse later.
